ticket.title: Publish a period.closed audit event when a period is closed
ticket.why: Closing a period is the one bookkeeping action with no audit trail. Auditors asked who closed each period and when, and today the answer is only in the request logs.
ticket.what: In `src/ledger/services/periods.py`, `close_period` publishes `period.closed` on the event bus with `{tenant_id, period_id, closed_by}` after the close row is written. Nothing else changes.
acceptance: Closing a period publishes exactly one `period.closed` event carrying tenant_id, period_id and closed_by.
A failing subscriber does not roll back the close.
No event is published when the close itself fails.

file.patch:
diff --git a/src/ledger/services/periods.py b/src/ledger/services/periods.py
index 5c1a2f0..9e7d3b4 100644
--- a/src/ledger/services/periods.py
+++ b/src/ledger/services/periods.py
@@ -1,13 +1,66 @@
 """Period service: opening and closing bookkeeping periods."""
 from __future__ import annotations
 
+from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+from typing import Callable, Mapping
+
+from ledger import settings
 from ledger.errors import LedgerError
+from ledger.integration import bus
 from ledger.storage import store
 from ledger.types import Period, User
 
 
+class AuditEventFactory(ABC):
+    """Builds the topic and payload for one kind of audit event."""
+
+    @abstractmethod
+    def topic(self, action: str) -> str: ...
+
+    @abstractmethod
+    def payload(self, period: Period, user: User) -> dict: ...
+
+
+@dataclass
+class PeriodEventPolicy:
+    """Configurable policy for which period events are published and how."""
+
+    enabled: bool = True
+    topic_prefix: str = "period"
+    payload_builders: Mapping[str, Callable[[Period, User], dict]] = field(default_factory=dict)
+    publisher: Callable[[str, dict], None] = bus.publish
+
+
+class DefaultPeriodEventFactory(AuditEventFactory):
+    def __init__(self, policy: PeriodEventPolicy | None = None) -> None:
+        self.policy = policy or PeriodEventPolicy()
+
+    def topic(self, action: str) -> str:
+        return f"{self.policy.topic_prefix}.{action}"
+
+    def payload(self, period: Period, user: User) -> dict:
+        builder = self.policy.payload_builders.get("closed", _default_payload)
+        return builder(period, user)
+
+
+def _default_payload(period: Period, user: User) -> dict:
+    return {"tenant_id": period.tenant_id, "period_id": period.id, "closed_by": user.id}
+
+
+def _factory() -> AuditEventFactory:
+    name = getattr(settings, "AUDIT_EVENT_STRATEGY", "default")
+    return _FACTORIES[name]()
+
+
+_FACTORIES: dict[str, Callable[[], AuditEventFactory]] = {"default": DefaultPeriodEventFactory}
+
+
 def close_period(period: Period, user: User) -> None:
     """Close ``period`` by writing its close row."""
     if period.closed:
         raise PeriodClosedError(f"period {period.id} is already closed")
     store.close_period(period, user)
+    factory = _factory()
+    if factory and getattr(factory, "policy", PeriodEventPolicy()).enabled:
+        bus.publish(factory.topic("closed"), factory.payload(period, user))

rules.text: Interface code never calls the store directly; it goes through a service.
Every write to the ledger goes through `post_entry`, which enforces double entry.
The storage layer is the only layer that contains SQL.
Cross-cutting side effects (audit, email) are published on the event bus, not called inline.
Reports read from the reporting views, never from the entries table.
Money is handled as integer minor units; a float never reaches the storage layer.

conventions.text: Public functions in production modules carry type hints and a one-line docstring; test functions in `test_*.py` are exempt.
Errors are raised as `LedgerError` subclasses; handlers translate them, services never catch broadly.
Tests live next to the module they cover as `test_<module>.py` and run with pytest.
Commit messages are imperative and under 72 characters on the first line.
Log lines are structured key=value pairs, never f-strings with embedded values.

components.name: API router
components.provides: Maps HTTP routes to service calls and turns service errors into JSON error responses.

components.name: Auth
components.provides: Session cookie and API token authentication as router middleware; loads the current tenant.

components.name: Cache helper
components.provides: A TTL cache in front of Postgres store reads, keyed by query name and parameters, invalidated on every write through post_entry.
components.interface: get(key) -> value | None; set(key, value, ttl_s=60); invalidate(prefix)

components.name: CSV importer
components.provides: Parses bank statement CSV files into candidate entries and posts them through post_entry after matching rules.

components.name: Event bus
components.provides: An in-process publish/subscribe bus for audit, email and webhook side effects, drained after each request.

components.name: Invoice renderer
components.provides: Renders invoices to HTML and PDF from a period's entries using server-side templates.

components.name: Ledger CLI
components.provides: Command-line entry point for posting entries, closing periods and running imports against a local or remote Ledger.

components.name: Postgres store
components.provides: All SQL for entries, periods, tenants and reporting views; the only module that opens a database connection.
